title: Home Purchase Financing Returned-Payment Fee — Repeat Return Multiplier
content:
**Training note: the repeat return multiplier (Home Purchase Financing)**

**What is the repeat return multiplier?** It is the multiplier applied to the return channel charge of a returned-payment fee according to how many returns are counted on the loan for that fee. Where three or more returns are counted, the return repeat multiplier is 1.5; where exactly two returns are counted, it is 1.25. With fewer than two returns counted, no repeat multiplier applies.

**Does the return being charged count?** Yes. Every return in the counting period counts, the return being charged among them.

**What does the multiplier act on?** The return channel charge only. The return reason charge is added to the multiplied channel charge, not multiplied, and the fee is rounded half up to the cent once, on that sum.

| Returns counted | Return repeat multiplier |
|---|---|
| 3 or more | 1.5 |
| exactly 2 | 1.25 |
| 1 or none | none applies |

**Worked example (hypothetical figures).** A return channel charge of 20.00 with exactly two returns counted becomes 20.00 times 1.25, that is 25.00; with a return reason charge of 5.00 added the fee is 30.00. With three returns counted the channel charge becomes 30.00 and the fee 35.00.
